source.text: Ἐπειδὴ ἐπλήρωσεν πάντα τὰ ῥήματα αὐτοῦ εἰς τὰς ἀκοὰς τοῦ λαοῦ, εἰσῆλθεν εἰς Καφαρναούμ.

records.literal_gloss: When he had completed all the words of him in the hearing of the people, he entered into Capernaum.

en.L: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had completed all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} words in the hearing of the people, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} entered into Capernaum.
en.B: When Jesus had finished saying all these things to the people who were listening, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went into Capernaum.
en.R: Jesus finished teaching the people. Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to the town of Capernaum.

fr.L: Lorsqu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} eut achevé toutes {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} paroles aux oreilles du peuple, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans Capharnaüm.
fr.B: Quand Jésus eut fini de dire tout cela au peuple qui l’écoutait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} entra dans Capharnaüm.
fr.R: Jésus a fini d’enseigner les gens. Ensuite, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est allé dans la ville de Capharnaüm.

decisions.choice: all his words: the teaching of 6:20-49
decisions.reason: The sentence closes the sermon of chapter 6 and moves to a new scene. "In the hearing of the people" recalls that the crowd, not only the disciples, heard it (6:17-19).

decisions.choice: Capernaum: a town on the north shore of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Jesus made the town a base for his work in Galilee (4:31).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Luke's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("dit-il", 7:40) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As in John and Mark: the passé simple is the normal tense of written narrative and suits a careful public reading; Readable tells the story in the passé composé, as French is spoken and read in school today. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level, and the parable of 7:41-42 is told in the passé composé, as speech.

decisions.choice: every French pronoun for Jesus carries the deity_pronoun span, subject "il" included (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: French must write the subject pronoun, so "il" for Jesus carries the span wherever the English "he" does, and also where French needs a pronoun the English lacks ("l’accompagnaient", 7:11). When people speak to Jesus they say "tu", and "tu", "te", "toi" carry the span; when Jesus speaks of himself, "moi", "me", "mes" do, but "je" does not. A pronoun at the start of a sentence is written plainly with its capital.

source.text: Ἑκατοντάρχου δέ τινος δοῦλος κακῶς ἔχων ἤμελλεν τελευτᾶν, ὃς ἦν αὐτῷ ἔντιμος.

records.literal_gloss: Of a centurion then a certain slave being ill was about to die, who was to him highly valued.

en.L: Now a certain centurion's slave, who was highly valued by him, was sick and about to die.
en.B: There was a centurion whose servant was very dear to him, and the servant was ill and close to death.
en.R: An army officer called a centurion lived there. He had a servant whom he valued very much. The servant was sick and about to die.

fr.L: Or l’esclave d’un certain centurion, qui lui était très précieux, était malade et sur le point de mourir.
fr.B: Un centurion avait un serviteur qui lui était très cher. Ce serviteur était malade, sur le point de mourir.
fr.R: Dans cette ville vivait un officier de l’armée romaine qu’on appelait un centurion. Il avait un serviteur qui comptait beaucoup pour lui. Ce serviteur était malade et allait bientôt mourir.

decisions.choice: centurion: an army officer in command of about a hundred soldiers
decisions.reason: The title means the commander of a hundred. Galilee was ruled by Herod Antipas (3:1), whose troops were organized in the Roman way. The centurion was a Gentile, not a Jew: the Jewish elders speak of "our nation" as if it were not his (7:5).

decisions.choice: slave: a person who belonged to his master
decisions.reason: The word is the usual word for a slave, as in 2:29. The slave was his master's property, not a paid worker. In 7:7 the centurion calls him by another word, see the note there.

decisions.choice: highly valued: dear to his master, and also of great worth to him
decisions.reason: The word means held in honor or prized. It can describe something precious (1 Peter 2:4, 6). The centurion's concern shows that the slave mattered to him as a person.

decisions.choice: an army officer called a centurion lived there
decisions.reason: Readable says what a centurion was, and places him in Capernaum, as 7:1 implies.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

decisions.choice: un centurion (L, B); un officier de l’armée romaine qu’on appelait un centurion (R) (for the whole chapter)
alternatives: un officier romain at every level
decisions.reason: "Centurion" is the French word for the Roman rank. Readable explains it on first mention, as the English Readable does, and then says "le centurion".

decisions.choice: esclave (L); serviteur (B, R) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As the English and the style guide: Literal keeps "esclave"; Balanced and Readable say "serviteur", while the meaning decision keeps that the man was owned.

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ περὶ τοῦ Ἰησοῦ ἀπέστειλεν πρὸς αὐτὸν πρεσβυτέρους τῶν Ἰουδαίων, ἐρωτῶν αὐτὸν ὅπως ἐλθὼν διασώσῃ τὸν δοῦλον αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then about Jesus he sent to him elders of the Jews, asking him that having come he might save the slave of him.

en.L: And having heard about Jesus, he sent to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} elders of the Jews, asking {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come and save his slave.
en.B: He heard about Jesus and sent some Jewish elders to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, to ask {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to come and save his servant's life.
en.R: The centurion heard about Jesus. So he sent some leaders of the Jews to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He wanted them to ask Jesus to come and make his servant well.

fr.L: Et ayant entendu parler de Jésus, il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoya des anciens des Juifs, {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} priant de venir sauver son esclave.
fr.B: Il entendit parler de Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} envoya quelques anciens des Juifs pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander de venir sauver la vie de son serviteur.
fr.R: Le centurion a entendu parler de Jésus. Alors il {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} a envoyé quelques responsables des Juifs. Il voulait qu’ils demandent à Jésus de venir guérir son serviteur.

decisions.choice: elders of the Jews: respected older men who led the Jewish community of the town
alternatives: members of the ruling council in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Each Jewish town had its elders, who settled local matters and led the synagogue community. The centurion does not come himself but sends men whom Jesus, a Jew, would trust.

decisions.choice: save: bring safely through, here from death
decisions.reason: The verb means to rescue someone all the way through a danger. The slave is about to die (7:2), and the request is that his life be saved.

decisions.choice: his slave: the same word as in 7:2
decisions.reason: Luke keeps the word for slave in 7:2, 3, 8 and 10.

decisions.choice: make his servant well
decisions.reason: Readable says what saving the servant meant here: healing him before he died.

decisions.choice: leaders of the Jews
decisions.reason: Today "elders" suggests only age or a church office. Readable says what they were.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m3) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: οἱ δὲ παραγενόμενοι πρὸς τὸν Ἰησοῦν παρεκάλουν αὐτὸν σπουδαίως λέγοντες ὅτι Ἄξιός ἐστιν ᾧ παρέξῃ τοῦτο, ἀγαπᾷ γὰρ τὸ ἔθνος ἡμῶν καὶ τὴν συναγωγὴν αὐτὸς ᾠκοδόμησεν ἡμῖν.

records.literal_gloss: And having come to Jesus they were begging him earnestly saying that, Worthy he is for whom you will grant this, \v 5 he loves for the nation of us and the synagogue he built for us.

en.L: And when they came to Jesus, they begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} earnestly, saying, "He is worthy for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to grant this to him, \v 5 for he loves our nation, and he himself built the synagogue for us."
en.B: They came to Jesus and pleaded with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} urgently. "He deserves to have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do this for him," they said. \v 5 "He loves our people, and he is the one who built our synagogue for us."
en.R: They came to Jesus and begged {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to help. They said, "This man deserves {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} help. \v 5 He loves our people, and he even paid to build our synagogue."

fr.L: Et arrivés auprès de Jésus, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suppliaient instamment, disant : « Il est digne que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} lui accordes cela, \v 5 car il aime notre nation, et la synagogue, c’est lui qui nous l’a bâtie. »
fr.B: Arrivés auprès de Jésus, ils {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} supplièrent avec insistance : « Il mérite que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} fasses cela pour lui, dirent-ils. \v 5 Il aime notre peuple, et c’est lui qui a construit notre synagogue pour nous. »
fr.R: Ils sont venus trouver Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}ont supplié d’intervenir. Ils ont dit : « Cet homme mérite que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} l’aides. \v 5 Il aime notre peuple, et il a même payé la construction de notre synagogue. »

decisions.choice: worthy: deserving, because of what he has done
decisions.reason: The elders argue from the centurion's good deeds. In 7:6-7 the centurion says the opposite of himself: he is not worthy. The two words come from the same root.

decisions.choice: he loves our nation and built our synagogue: a Gentile friendly to the Jews and their worship
decisions.reason: Some Gentiles honored the God of Israel and supported the synagogue without becoming Jews, like Cornelius, another centurion (Acts 10:1-2, 22). The elders do not say he had become a Jew.

decisions.choice: he himself built: he paid for the building
alternatives: he built it with his own hands
decisions.reason: The pronoun stresses that it was his gift. A wealthy patron "built" by paying for the work.

decisions.choice: the request in two sentences
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable break the elders' words into shorter sentences.

decisions.choice: paid to build
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the centurion paid for the building, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: "tu" when people speak to Jesus, here the elders ("que tu lui accordes cela")
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the whole Bible: one person is addressed as "tu", Jesus included, even by respectful strangers such as the elders and the centurion's friends. A "vous" of politeness would bring in a register the Greek does not mark.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς ἐπορεύετο σὺν αὐτοῖς.

records.literal_gloss: And Jesus was going with them.

en.L: And Jesus was going with them.
en.B: So Jesus went with them.
en.R: So Jesus went with them.

fr.L: Et Jésus allait avec eux.
fr.B: Jésus partit donc avec eux.
fr.R: Alors Jésus est parti avec eux.

decisions.choice: was going: Jesus was on his way
decisions.reason: The tense describes the journey under way. Before Jesus reaches the house, the centurion sends a second message (7:6).

source.text: ἤδη δὲ αὐτοῦ οὐ μακρὰν ἀπέχοντος ἀπὸ τῆς οἰκίας ἔπεμψεν φίλους ὁ ἑκατοντάρχης λέγων αὐτῷ· Κύριε, μὴ σκύλλου, οὐ γὰρ ἱκανός εἰμι ἵνα ὑπὸ τὴν στέγην μου εἰσέλθῃς·

records.literal_gloss: Already then him not far being distant from the house sent friends the centurion saying to him, Lord, not trouble yourself, not for worthy I am that under the roof of me you should come;

en.L: And when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was already not far from the house, the centurion sent friends, saying to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, do not trouble {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}, for I am not worthy for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to come under my roof;
en.B: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was not far from the house, the centurion sent friends to say to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, do not put {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}} to any trouble. I am not worthy to have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come under my roof.
en.R: Jesus was getting close to the house when the centurion sent some friends with a message for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They told {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, "Lord, do not trouble {{deity_pronoun:yourself|Yourself}}. I am not good enough to have {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} come into my house.

fr.L: Et comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} n’était déjà plus loin de la maison, le centurion envoya des amis {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dire : « Seigneur, ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dérange pas, car je ne suis pas digne que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} entres sous mon toit ;
fr.B: Il n’était plus très loin de la maison quand le centurion envoya des amis {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} dire : « Seigneur, ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} donne pas cette peine. Je ne suis pas digne de {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} recevoir sous mon toit.
fr.R: Jésus approchait de la maison quand le centurion a envoyé des amis avec un message pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Ils {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Seigneur, ne {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} dérange pas. Je ne mérite pas que {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} entres dans ma maison.

decisions.choice: Lord: a title of respect that, in Luke's telling, says more than "sir"
decisions.reason: The word can be a polite address. But the centurion speaks of Jesus's word as having power to command a sickness (7:7-8). Luke's readers hear the title he uses for God and for Jesus (2:11).

decisions.choice: come under my roof: enter my house
alternatives: a fear of being made unclean himself
decisions.reason: Devout Jews avoided entering a Gentile's house, because it would make them ritually unclean (Acts 10:28; 11:2-3). The centurion knows this, but he also speaks of his own unworthiness: he will not ask Jesus to come.

decisions.choice: trouble yourself: put yourself to effort, be bothered
decisions.reason: The verb first meant to harass or wear out. Here it is a courteous phrase: do not go to the trouble.

decisions.choice: saying to him: the friends speak the centurion's words
alternatives: the centurion came and spoke himself
decisions.reason: The centurion speaks through his friends, as he first spoke through the elders (7:3). Matthew tells the story more briefly, as if the centurion spoke in person (Matthew 8:5-13).

decisions.choice: I am not good enough to have you come into my house
alternatives: I am not worthy that you should come under my roof
decisions.reason: Readable explains the idiom of the roof.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:8
alternatives: a separate quotation in each verse
decisions.reason: The centurion's message runs on through 7:7-8 as one speech.

decisions.choice: Seigneur
decisions.reason: As the meaning decision says, in Luke's telling the centurion's address means more than "sir"; "Seigneur" keeps that, as "Lord" does in English. "Maître" is kept for "Teacher" (7:40).

source.text: διὸ οὐδὲ ἐμαυτὸν ἠξίωσα πρὸς σὲ ἐλθεῖν· ἀλλὰ εἰπὲ λόγῳ, καὶ ἰαθήτω ὁ παῖς μου·

records.literal_gloss: Therefore neither myself I considered worthy to you to come; but say in a word, and let be healed the servant of me.

en.L: Therefore neither did I consider myself worthy to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; but say with a word, and let my servant be healed.
en.B: That is why I did not think myself fit to come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} myself. Only speak a command, and let my servant be healed.
en.R: That is why I did not come to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} myself. Just give the order, and my servant will be well.

fr.L: C’est pourquoi je ne me suis pas non plus jugé digne de venir vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; mais dis un mot, et que mon serviteur soit guéri ;
fr.B: C’est pourquoi je ne me suis pas cru digne de venir moi-même jusqu’à {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Donne seulement un ordre, et que mon serviteur soit guéri.
fr.R: C’est pour cela que je ne suis pas venu {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} voir moi-même. Donne simplement l’ordre, et mon serviteur sera guéri.

decisions.choice: servant: the same slave as in 7:2, called by a word of the household
decisions.reason: The word can mean a child, a boy, or a slave of any age; masters often called a household slave "boy". Luke has already said that the sick man is a slave (7:2, 3) and will say so again (7:10), so here it is not a son. The centurion uses the warmer household word, which matches how dear the slave was to him.

decisions.choice: say with a word: give a command, without coming
decisions.reason: The centurion believes Jesus's spoken order is enough, even at a distance. The following verse explains why.

decisions.choice: let him be healed: a command form, confident of the result
alternatives: a wish: may he be healed
decisions.reason: The form is an imperative. The centurion speaks of the healing as sure to follow the command.

decisions.choice: let him be healed, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: he will be healed, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Several early manuscripts have the command form; many others have the future, as in Matthew 8:8. The meaning is close either way. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: A different Greek word from the one in 7:2, which Literal renders "slave"; Balanced and Readable have "servant" for both, since the same man is meant. "Boy" would suggest a child, which Luke's other verses rule out.

decisions.choice: Just give the order
decisions.reason: Readable says what speaking a word means here.

source.text: καὶ γὰρ ἐγὼ ἄνθρωπός εἰμι ὑπὸ ἐξουσίαν τασσόμενος, ἔχων ὑπ’ ἐμαυτὸν στρατιώτας, καὶ λέγω τούτῳ· Πορεύθητι, καὶ πορεύεται, καὶ ἄλλῳ· Ἔρχου, καὶ ἔρχεται, καὶ τῷ δούλῳ μου· Ποίησον τοῦτο, καὶ ποιεῖ.

records.literal_gloss: Also for I a man am under authority being placed, having under myself soldiers, and I say to this one, Go, and he goes, and to another, Come, and he comes, and to the slave of me, Do this, and he does.

en.L: For I also am a man placed under authority, having soldiers under me, and I say to this one, 'Go,' and he goes, and to another, 'Come,' and he comes, and to my slave, 'Do this,' and he does [it]."
en.B: For I myself serve under men who have authority over me, and I have soldiers under my command. I say to one, 'Go!' and off he goes; to another, 'Come here!' and he comes; and to my servant, 'Do this!' and he does it."
en.R: I know about giving orders. I have officers over me, and I have soldiers who obey me. I tell one soldier, 'Go!' and he goes. I tell another, 'Come here!' and he comes. I tell my servant, 'Do this!' and he does it."

fr.L: Car moi aussi, je suis un homme placé sous une autorité, ayant sous moi des soldats, et je dis à celui-ci : “Va”, et il va, et à un autre : “Viens”, et il vient, et à mon esclave : “Fais ceci”, et il [le] fait. »
fr.B: Moi-même, en effet, je suis sous les ordres de chefs qui ont autorité sur moi, et j’ai des soldats sous mes ordres. Je dis à l’un : “Va !”, et il part ; à un autre : “Viens ici !”, et il vient ; et à mon serviteur : “Fais cela !”, et il le fait. »
fr.R: Je sais ce que c’est que de donner des ordres. J’ai des chefs au-dessus de moi, et j’ai des soldats qui m’obéissent. Je dis à un soldat : “Va !”, et il va. Je dis à un autre : “Viens ici !”, et il vient. Je dis à mon serviteur : “Fais ceci !”, et il le fait. »

decisions.choice: I also am under authority: like Jesus, he stands in a chain of command
alternatives: I am a man of authority
decisions.reason: The centurion reasons from his own life. He obeys those above him and is obeyed by those below him; his word carries the authority of his superiors. So Jesus's word carries God's authority, and sickness must obey it.

decisions.choice: my slave: a slave of his household
decisions.reason: The word is the one used in 7:2 for a slave. The centurion is not necessarily speaking of the sick man.

decisions.choice: I know about giving orders. I have officers over me
alternatives: I also am a man placed under authority
decisions.reason: Readable states the point of the comparison in plain words.

decisions.choice: Come here!
decisions.reason: The command in English needs "here" to sound natural.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable, as the style guide has it; the meaning decision (m2) keeps that the person was owned, and Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: ἀκούσας δὲ ταῦτα ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἐθαύμασεν αὐτόν, καὶ στραφεὶς τῷ ἀκολουθοῦντι αὐτῷ ὄχλῳ εἶπεν· Λέγω ὑμῖν, οὐδὲ ἐν τῷ Ἰσραὴλ τοσαύτην πίστιν εὗρον.

records.literal_gloss: Having heard then these things Jesus marveled at him, and having turned to the following him crowd he said, I say to you, not even in the Israel such great faith did I find.

en.L: And hearing these things, Jesus marveled at him, and turning to the crowd that was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you, not even in Israel have I found such great faith."
en.B: When Jesus heard this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was amazed at the man. Turning to the crowd that followed {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "I tell you, I have not found faith this great even in Israel."
en.R: Jesus was amazed when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} heard this. He turned to the crowd that was following {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} and said, "I tell you, not even among God's people in Israel have I seen faith as strong as this man's!"

fr.L: En entendant cela, Jésus fut étonné de lui, et se retournant vers la foule qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je vous le dis, même en Israël je n’ai pas trouvé une si grande foi. »
fr.B: Quand Jésus entendit ces paroles, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fut émerveillé par cet homme. Se tournant vers la foule qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivait, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Je vous le dis : même en Israël, je n’ai pas trouvé une foi aussi grande. »
fr.R: Jésus a été très étonné quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a entendu cela. Il s’est tourné vers la foule qui {{deity_pronoun:le|Le}} suivait et a dit : « Je vous le dis, même parmi le peuple de Dieu, en Israël, je n’ai jamais vu une foi aussi forte que celle de cet homme ! »

decisions.choice: marveled: was amazed
decisions.reason: The Gospels seldom say that Jesus was amazed. Mark 6:6 says he was amazed at the unbelief in his hometown; here a Gentile's trust amazes him.

decisions.choice: faith: trust in Jesus's power and authority to heal by his word
decisions.reason: The centurion's faith is his confidence that Jesus's command will be obeyed (7:7-8). In Luke faith is trust in Jesus shown in action (5:20; 7:50).

decisions.choice: not even in Israel: a Gentile's faith surpasses what Jesus has met among God's own people
decisions.reason: Simeon sang that Jesus would be a light for the Gentiles (2:32). Jesus said that Elijah and Elisha were sent to foreigners (4:25-27).

decisions.choice: among God's people in Israel
decisions.reason: Readable says what Israel means here: the people, not only the land.

decisions.choice: faith as strong as this man's
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the key term faith and makes the comparison plain.

source.text: καὶ ὑποστρέψαντες εἰς τὸν οἶκον οἱ πεμφθέντες εὗρον τὸν δοῦλον ὑγιαίνοντα.

records.literal_gloss: And having returned to the house those having been sent found the slave in good health.

en.L: And when those who had been sent returned to the house, they found the slave in good health.
en.B: When the messengers went back to the house, they found the servant well.
en.R: The men who had been sent went back to the centurion's house. They found that the servant was well again.

fr.L: Et de retour à la maison, ceux qui avaient été envoyés trouvèrent l’esclave en bonne santé.
fr.B: Quand les messagers rentrèrent à la maison, ils trouvèrent le serviteur en pleine santé.
fr.R: Les hommes qui avaient été envoyés sont retournés à la maison du centurion. Ils ont vu que le serviteur était de nouveau en bonne santé.

decisions.choice: in good health: fully healthy
decisions.reason: The word means sound and healthy (5:31). The slave who was about to die (7:2) is now well; Jesus never went to the house.

decisions.choice: those who had been sent: the friends of 7:6, and perhaps the elders too
decisions.reason: Luke does not say exactly who; it is the centurion's messengers.

decisions.choice: the centurion's house
decisions.reason: Readable says whose house it was.

decisions.choice: servant
decisions.reason: "Servant" in Balanced and Readable (style guide); Literal keeps "slave".

source.text: Καὶ ἐγένετο ἐν τῷ ἑξῆς ἐπορεύθη εἰς πόλιν καλουμένην Ναΐν, καὶ συνεπορεύοντο αὐτῷ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ ὄχλος πολύς.

records.literal_gloss: And it came about in the next [time] he went into a town being called Nain, and were going with him the disciples of him and a crowd great.

en.L: And it happened soon afterward [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went to a town called Nain, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples and a large crowd were going with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: Soon afterward Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and so did a large crowd.
en.R: Soon after this Jesus went to a town called Nain. His disciples went along with {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and a large crowd of people followed too.

fr.L: Et il arriva, peu après, qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se rendit dans une ville appelée Naïn, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples et une foule nombreuse faisaient route avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}.
fr.B: Peu après, Jésus se rendit dans une ville appelée Naïn. Ses disciples {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}accompagnaient, ainsi qu’une grande foule.
fr.R: Peu de temps après, Jésus est allé dans une ville appelée Naïn. Ses disciples sont partis avec {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, et une grande foule {{deity_pronoun:l’|L’}}a suivi aussi.

decisions.choice: soon afterward, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: on the next day, the reading of other manuscripts
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT has a form that means "in the time following". Other manuscripts have a form that means "on the next day". The two differ by one letter. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: Nain: a village in southern Galilee
decisions.reason: The Bible mentions Nain only here. It lay a few miles southeast of Nazareth, near the village of Shunem, where Elisha raised a woman's son (2 Kings 4:8-37).

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

source.text: ὡς δὲ ἤγγισεν τῇ πύλῃ τῆς πόλεως, καὶ ἰδοὺ ἐξεκομίζετο τεθνηκὼς μονογενὴς υἱὸς τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ αὐτὴ ἦν χήρα, καὶ ὄχλος τῆς πόλεως ἱκανὸς ἦν σὺν αὐτῇ.

records.literal_gloss: As then he drew near to the gate of the town, and look was being carried out having died an only son of the mother of him, and she was a widow, and a crowd of the town considerable was with her.

en.L: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came near the gate of the town, look, a man who had died was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a considerable crowd from the town was with her.
en.B: As {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} came near the town gate, a dead man was being carried out. He was his mother's only son, and she was a widow. A large crowd from the town was with her.
en.R: As Jesus came near the gate of the town, some people were carrying out a dead man to bury him. He was the only son of his mother, and her husband had died. Many people from the town were with her.

fr.L: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} approchait de la porte de la ville, voici qu’on emportait un mort, fils unique de sa mère, et elle était veuve ; et une foule considérable de la ville était avec elle.
fr.B: Comme {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} arrivait près de la porte de la ville, on emportait un mort. C’était le fils unique de sa mère, qui était veuve. Une foule nombreuse de la ville l’accompagnait.
fr.R: Quand Jésus est arrivé près de la porte de la ville, des gens sortaient un mort pour aller l’enterrer. C’était le fils unique de sa mère, et le mari de cette femme était mort. Beaucoup de gens de la ville étaient avec elle.

decisions.choice: being carried out: taken out of the town for burial
decisions.reason: Burials took place outside towns, usually on the day of death. The body was carried on an open frame, with the family and mourners following.

decisions.choice: only: the one and only son
decisions.reason: The word means the only one of its kind (8:42; 9:38). Luke uses it of an only child.

decisions.choice: a widow: a woman whose husband has died, now without her son as well
alternatives: a woman living alone by choice
decisions.reason: With no husband and no son, she had lost those who would provide for and protect her. The law tells God's people to care for widows (Deuteronomy 24:17-21).

decisions.choice: a widow's only son: the story recalls Elijah at Zarephath
decisions.reason: Elijah met a widow at the town gate and raised her son (1 Kings 17:10, 17-24). Jesus has already pointed to that widow (4:25-26). 7:15 uses the words of 1 Kings 17:23.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

decisions.choice: to bury him
decisions.reason: Readable says why the body was being carried out.

decisions.choice: her husband had died
decisions.reason: Readable says what being a widow means.

decisions.choice: voici (L); not rendered as a separate word (B, R) (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: Unlike the English "behold", French "voici" is still a living word for pointing to what comes next, so Literal uses it for Luke's attention word (also 7:25, 7:27, 7:34, 7:37). Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν ὁ κύριος ἐσπλαγχνίσθη ἐπ’ αὐτῇ καὶ εἶπεν αὐτῇ· Μὴ κλαῖε.

records.literal_gloss: And having seen her the Lord felt compassion on her and said to her, Not weep.

en.L: And seeing her, the Lord had compassion on her and said to her, "Do not weep."
en.B: When the Lord saw her, pity for her moved {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} deeply, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to her, "Stop weeping."
en.R: When the Lord Jesus saw her, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} felt very sorry for her. He said to her, "Do not cry."

fr.L: Et la voyant, le Seigneur fut ému de compassion pour elle et lui dit : « Ne pleure pas. »
fr.B: En la voyant, le Seigneur fut saisi d’une profonde pitié pour elle, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Ne pleure plus. »
fr.R: Quand le Seigneur Jésus l’a vue, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} a eu beaucoup de peine pour elle. Il lui a dit : « Ne pleure pas. »

decisions.choice: the Lord: Luke the narrator calls Jesus by the title used for God
decisions.reason: This is the first time Luke himself, telling the story, calls Jesus "the Lord". The angels announced him as Christ the Lord (2:11); Luke uses the title often from now on (7:19; 10:1).

decisions.choice: had compassion: felt a deep, inward pity that moves to action
alternatives: felt sorry in a distant way
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for the inner parts of the body, thought of as the seat of feeling (1:78). Luke uses it of the Samaritan (10:33) and the father of the lost son (15:20).

decisions.choice: do not weep: stop weeping
decisions.reason: The form tells someone to stop what they are already doing.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name so that a new reader knows who is meant.

decisions.choice: pity for her moved him deeply
alternatives: his heart went out to her
decisions.reason: Balanced gives the depth of the feeling in its own words.

decisions.choice: Ne pleure plus (B)
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the command as "stop weeping"; French "ne … plus" says that she is to stop, more gently than "arrête de pleurer".

source.text: καὶ προσελθὼν ἥψατο τῆς σοροῦ, οἱ δὲ βαστάζοντες ἔστησαν, καὶ εἶπεν· Νεανίσκε, σοὶ λέγω, ἐγέρθητι.

records.literal_gloss: And having come near he touched the bier, those then carrying stood still, and he said, Young man, to you I say, arise.

en.L: And coming near, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} touched the bier, and those carrying [it] stood still, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Young man, I say to you, arise."
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} went up and touched the bier, and the men carrying it stood still. He said, "Young man, I tell you, get up!"
en.R: Then Jesus went up and touched the frame they were carrying the body on. The men carrying it stopped. Jesus said, "Young man, I tell you, get up!"

fr.L: Et s’approchant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} toucha la civière, et ceux qui [la] portaient s’arrêtèrent, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} dit : « Jeune homme, je te le dis, lève-toi. »
fr.B: Puis {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} s’approcha et toucha la civière, et ceux qui la portaient s’arrêtèrent. Il dit : « Jeune homme, je te le dis, lève-toi ! »
fr.R: Ensuite, Jésus s’est approché et a touché le brancard sur lequel on portait le corps. Les hommes qui le portaient se sont arrêtés. Jésus a dit : « Jeune homme, je te le dis, lève-toi ! »

decisions.choice: bier: the open frame or stretcher on which the body was carried
decisions.reason: Jewish burials did not use closed coffins; the body, wrapped in cloth, lay on an open bier. Touching it would make a person unclean under the law (Numbers 19:11-16), but Jesus's touch brings life.

decisions.choice: arise: get up, be raised
decisions.reason: The verb is used of getting up and of being raised from the dead (7:22; 9:22).

decisions.choice: to you I say: Jesus commands by his own authority
decisions.reason: Elijah and Elisha prayed to the LORD before the dead were raised (1 Kings 17:20-21; 2 Kings 4:33). Jesus speaks directly to the dead man.

decisions.choice: the frame they were carrying the body on
decisions.reason: "Bier" is a rare word, and "coffin" would be wrong.

decisions.choice: la civière (L, B); le brancard sur lequel on portait le corps (R)
decisions.reason: The body lay on an open frame (m1). "Cercueil" and "bière" are closed coffins, which would be wrong. "Civière" is the usual word for a stretcher carried by hand; Readable describes it, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ ἀνεκάθισεν ὁ νεκρὸς καὶ ἤρξατο λαλεῖν, καὶ ἔδωκεν αὐτὸν τῇ μητρὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And sat up the dead [man] and began to speak, and he gave him to the mother of him.

en.L: And the dead man sat up and began to speak, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave him to his mother.
en.B: The dead man sat up and began to talk, and Jesus gave him back to his mother.
en.R: The dead man sat up and began to talk! And Jesus gave him back to his mother.

fr.L: Et le mort se redressa et commença à parler, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} le donna à sa mère.
fr.B: Le mort se redressa et se mit à parler, et Jésus le rendit à sa mère.
fr.R: Le mort s’est assis et il a commencé à parler ! Et Jésus l’a rendu à sa mère.

decisions.choice: he gave him to his mother: the words of 1 Kings 17:23
decisions.reason: The Greek Old Testament uses the same words of Elijah, who gave the widow's son back to his mother. The people's response in 7:16 names Jesus a great prophet.

decisions.choice: began to speak: proof that he was truly alive
decisions.reason: Luke does not tell what he said; his speaking shows that life has returned.

decisions.choice: Jesus gave him back
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus, since several men have been mentioned, and say "back" because she had lost him.

source.text: ἔλαβεν δὲ φόβος πάντας, καὶ ἐδόξαζον τὸν θεὸν λέγοντες ὅτι Προφήτης μέγας ἠγέρθη ἐν ἡμῖν, καὶ ὅτι Ἐπεσκέψατο ὁ θεὸς τὸν λαὸν αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Seized then fear all, and they were glorifying the God saying that, A prophet great has been raised among us, and that, Has visited the God the people of him.

en.L: And fear seized [them] all, and they were glorifying God, saying, "A great prophet has been raised up among us," and, "God has visited {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people!"
en.B: Awe took hold of everyone, and they gave glory to God. "A great prophet has appeared among us!" they said, and, "God has come to help {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people!"
en.R: Everyone there was filled with fear and wonder, and they gave glory to God. They said, "A great prophet has come to us!" They also said, "God has come to help {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people!"

fr.L: Et la crainte s’empara de tous, et ils glorifiaient Dieu, disant : « Un grand prophète a été suscité parmi nous », et : « Dieu a visité {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple ! »
fr.B: Une crainte pleine de respect s’empara de tous, et ils rendaient gloire à Dieu. « Un grand prophète est apparu parmi nous ! » disaient-ils, et : « Dieu est venu au secours de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple ! »
fr.R: Tous ceux qui étaient là ont été remplis de crainte et d’émerveillement, et ils ont rendu gloire à Dieu. Ils ont dit : « Un grand prophète est venu parmi nous ! » Ils ont dit aussi : « Dieu est venu au secours de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} peuple ! »

decisions.choice: fear: awe before God's power
decisions.reason: As in 5:26, people are filled with fear when God acts among them.

decisions.choice: glorifying God: praising God for what he has done
decisions.reason: People in Luke give glory to God when they see his work (2:20; 5:25-26).

decisions.choice: has been raised up: God has sent a prophet
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 7:14, but here it means that God has caused a prophet to appear, as Moses promised (Deuteronomy 18:15).

decisions.choice: visited: came to help
decisions.reason: As in 1:68 and 1:78, God visits his people when he comes to act for them (Exodus 4:31; Ruth 1:6).

decisions.choice: gave glory to God
decisions.reason: The verb is the one for glory; Balanced and Readable keep that word, as in 5:25.

decisions.choice: has come to help his people
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give the sense of "visited", as in 1:68.

decisions.choice: awe (B); fear and wonder (R)
decisions.reason: As in 5:26, "fear" alone would suggest terror.

decisions.choice: une crainte pleine de respect (B); la crainte et l’émerveillement (R)
decisions.reason: As the English: the fear is awe before God's power (m1). "La peur" would say terror; Literal keeps "la crainte", and Balanced and Readable say what kind of fear it was.

source.text: καὶ ἐξῆλθεν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ἐν ὅλῃ τῇ Ἰουδαίᾳ περὶ αὐτοῦ καὶ πάσῃ τῇ περιχώρῳ.

records.literal_gloss: And went out the report this in all the Judea concerning him and all the surrounding region.

en.L: And this report about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} went out in all Judea and all the surrounding region.
en.B: This news about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} spread through all Judea and the whole region around it.
en.R: The news about what Jesus had done spread everywhere in the land of the Jews and in all the places around it.

fr.L: Et cette nouvelle à {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} sujet se répandit dans toute la Judée et dans toute la région d’alentour.
fr.B: Ce qu’on disait de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} se répandit dans toute la Judée et dans toute la région voisine.
fr.R: La nouvelle de ce que Jésus avait fait s’est répandue partout dans le pays des Juifs et dans toutes les régions autour.

decisions.choice: Judea: the whole land of the Jews
alternatives: only the southern region around Jerusalem
decisions.reason: Nain is in Galilee, so Judea here means the land where the Jews lived, as in 1:5 and 4:44.

decisions.choice: report: the word that was told about him
decisions.reason: The noun is the usual word for word or message; here it is the news that spread by word of mouth.

decisions.choice: the land of the Jews
decisions.reason: Readable explains the broad sense of Judea, as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: what Jesus had done
decisions.reason: Readable says what the news was about.

source.text: Καὶ ἀπήγγειλαν Ἰωάννῃ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ περὶ πάντων τούτων.

records.literal_gloss: And reported to John the disciples of him concerning all these things.

en.L: And John's disciples reported to him about all these things.
en.B: John's disciples told him about all these things.
en.R: John's followers told him about everything Jesus was doing.

fr.L: Et les disciples de Jean lui rapportèrent toutes ces choses.
fr.B: Les disciples de Jean lui racontèrent tout cela.
fr.R: Les disciples de Jean lui ont raconté tout ce que Jésus faisait.

decisions.choice: John: John the Baptist, now in prison
decisions.reason: Herod had locked John up in prison (3:19-20). His disciples still visited him.

decisions.choice: all these things: Jesus's healings and teaching, including the raising at Nain
decisions.reason: The phrase sums up what Luke has told since John's arrest.

decisions.choice: followers
decisions.reason: Readable uses an everyday word for disciples here, since they were not Jesus's disciples.

decisions.choice: everything Jesus was doing
decisions.reason: Readable says what "these things" were.

decisions.choice: les disciples de Jean at Readable too
decisions.reason: English Readable says "followers" because "disciples" sounds like Jesus's Twelve. In French "disciple" is the ordinary word for the pupil of any teacher, and "de Jean" makes plain whose they were, so Readable keeps it, as Mark's Readable keeps "disciples".

source.text: καὶ προσκαλεσάμενος δύο τινὰς τῶν μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ ὁ Ἰωάννης ἔπεμψεν πρὸς τὸν κύριον λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;

records.literal_gloss: And having called to [him] two certain of the disciples of him John \v 19 sent to the Lord saying, You are the coming [one] or another should we wait for?

en.L: And calling two of his disciples, John \v 19 sent [them] to the Lord, saying, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or should we wait for another?"
en.B: So John called two of his disciples \v 19 and sent them to the Lord to ask, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is to come, or are we to look for someone else?"
en.R: So John called two of his followers. \v 19 He sent them to the Lord Jesus to ask, "Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one God promised would come? Or should we keep waiting for someone else?"

fr.L: Et ayant appelé deux de ses disciples, Jean \v 19 [les] envoya vers le Seigneur pour dire : « Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui qui vient, ou devons-nous en attendre un autre ? »
fr.B: Jean appela donc deux de ses disciples \v 19 et les envoya demander au Seigneur : « Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui qui doit venir, ou devons-nous en attendre un autre ? »
fr.R: Alors Jean a appelé deux de ses disciples. \v 19 Il les a envoyés auprès du Seigneur Jésus pour {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} demander : « Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui que Dieu a promis d’envoyer ? Ou devons-nous continuer à attendre quelqu’un d’autre ? »

decisions.choice: the one who is coming: the one God promised to send
decisions.reason: John had said that one more powerful than he was coming (3:16). The prophets spoke of the LORD's messenger who comes (Malachi 3:1) and of the one who comes in the name of the LORD (Psalm 118:26; Luke 13:35).

decisions.choice: John's question: a real question, not a test for his disciples' sake
alternatives: John is sure and asks only for his disciples
decisions.reason: John had announced one who would judge with fire (3:16-17). Jesus is healing, not judging, and John is in prison. Jesus answers with what he is doing (7:22).

decisions.choice: the Lord, the reading of the SBLGNT
alternatives: Jesus, the reading of many manuscripts
decisions.reason: Many manuscripts read "Jesus"; several early ones read "the Lord". The person meant is the same. Reviewers should check the evidence against the apparatus.

decisions.choice: the one who is to come (B); the one who is coming (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced shows that his coming was promised.

decisions.choice: the one God promised would come
decisions.reason: Readable says why the one coming was expected, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: the Lord Jesus
decisions.reason: Readable adds the name, as in 7:13.

source.text: παραγενόμενοι δὲ πρὸς αὐτὸν οἱ ἄνδρες εἶπαν· Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς ἀπέστειλεν ἡμᾶς πρὸς σὲ λέγων· Σὺ εἶ ὁ ἐρχόμενος ἢ ἄλλον προσδοκῶμεν;

records.literal_gloss: Having come then to him the men said, John the Baptist has sent us to you saying, You are the coming [one] or another should we wait for?

en.L: And when the men had come to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they said, "John the Baptist has sent us to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, saying, 'Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is coming, or should we wait for another?'"
en.B: When the men reached {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, they said, "John the Baptist sent us to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to ask, 'Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one who is to come, or are we to look for someone else?'"
en.R: The men came to Jesus and said, "John the Baptist sent us to {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He wants to know, 'Are {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} the one God promised would come? Or should we keep waiting for someone else?'"

fr.L: Arrivés auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, les hommes dirent : « Jean le Baptiste nous a envoyés vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} pour dire : “Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui qui vient, ou devons-nous en attendre un autre ?” »
fr.B: Quand ils furent arrivés auprès de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, les hommes dirent : « Jean le Baptiste nous a envoyés vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} pour {{deity_pronoun:te|Te}} demander : “Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui qui doit venir, ou devons-nous en attendre un autre ?” »
fr.R: Les hommes sont venus trouver Jésus et {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} ont dit : « Jean le Baptiste nous a envoyés vers {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Il veut savoir : “Es-{{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} celui que Dieu a promis d’envoyer ? Ou devons-nous continuer à attendre quelqu’un d’autre ?” »

decisions.choice: the Baptist: the one who baptizes
alternatives: a member of a group called Baptists
decisions.reason: The title marks John by what he did (3:3). This is the first time Luke uses it (also 7:33; 9:19).

decisions.choice: the question repeated word for word
decisions.reason: Luke repeats John's question in full, which gives it weight.

decisions.choice: the one God promised would come
decisions.reason: As in 7:19.

decisions.choice: Jean le Baptiste (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the New Testament: the title says what John did, "the one who baptizes" (m1), which the hyphenated first name "Jean-Baptiste" hides.

source.text: ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ὥρᾳ ἐθεράπευσεν πολλοὺς ἀπὸ νόσων καὶ μαστίγων καὶ πνευμάτων πονηρῶν, καὶ τυφλοῖς πολλοῖς ἐχαρίσατο βλέπειν.

records.literal_gloss: In that the hour he healed many from diseases and afflictions and spirits evil, and to blind many he granted to see.

en.L: In that hour {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed many of diseases and afflictions and evil spirits, and to many blind [people] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} granted sight.
en.B: Just then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} healed many people of diseases, painful illnesses and evil spirits, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave many blind people the gift of sight.
en.R: At that very time Jesus was healing many people. Some had diseases or terrible pains, and some had evil spirits. Jesus also made many blind people able to see.

fr.L: À cette heure-là, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} guérit beaucoup [de gens] de maladies, d’infirmités et d’esprits mauvais, et à beaucoup d’aveugles {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} accorda de voir.
fr.B: Au même moment, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} guérit beaucoup de gens de leurs maladies, de leurs souffrances et des esprits mauvais, et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} fit à beaucoup d’aveugles le don de la vue.
fr.R: À ce moment-là, Jésus guérissait beaucoup de gens. Certains avaient des maladies ou de grandes douleurs, et d’autres avaient des esprits mauvais. Jésus a aussi permis à beaucoup d’aveugles de voir.

decisions.choice: afflictions: painful illnesses
decisions.reason: The word means a whip or a lash, and so a suffering that strikes like one (Mark 5:29, 34).

decisions.choice: granted: gave as a free gift
decisions.reason: The verb means to give freely, as a favor. It is used again in 7:42-43 of canceling a debt.

decisions.choice: in that hour: while John's messengers were there
decisions.reason: The healings take place before their eyes, so that they can tell John what they have seen (7:22).

decisions.choice: Jesus was healing
decisions.reason: Readable names Jesus and breaks the list into short sentences.

source.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς εἶπεν αὐτοῖς· Πορευθέντες ἀπαγγείλατε Ἰωάννῃ ἃ εἴδετε καὶ ἠκούσατε· τυφλοὶ ἀναβλέπουσιν, χωλοὶ περιπατοῦσιν, λεπροὶ καθαρίζονται, κωφοὶ ἀκούουσιν, νεκροὶ ἐγείρονται, πτωχοὶ εὐαγγελίζονται·

records.literal_gloss: And answering he said to them, Having gone report to John what you saw and heard: blind receive sight, lame walk, lepers are cleansed, deaf hear, dead are raised, poor have good news proclaimed;

en.L: And answering, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said to them, "Go and report to John what you have seen and heard: blind [people] receive sight, lame [people] walk, lepers are cleansed, and deaf [people] hear, dead [people] are raised, poor [people] have good news proclaimed [to them];
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} answered them, "Go back and tell John what you have seen and heard. The blind see again, the lame walk, people with leprosy are made clean, the deaf hear, the dead are raised, and the poor hear the good news.
en.R: Jesus answered John's followers, "Go back and tell John what you have seen and heard. Blind people can see. People who could not walk are walking. People with skin diseases are healed and made clean. Deaf people can hear. Dead people are raised to life. And poor people are hearing the good news.

fr.L: Et répondant, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur dit : « Allez rapporter à Jean ce que vous avez vu et entendu : des aveugles retrouvent la vue, des boiteux marchent, des lépreux sont purifiés, des sourds entendent, des morts sont ressuscités, à des pauvres la bonne nouvelle est annoncée ;
fr.B: Il leur répondit : « Retournez dire à Jean ce que vous avez vu et entendu. Les aveugles voient de nouveau, les boiteux marchent, les lépreux sont rendus purs, les sourds entendent, les morts sont ressuscités, et les pauvres entendent la bonne nouvelle.
fr.R: Jésus a répondu aux disciples de Jean : « Retournez dire à Jean ce que vous avez vu et entendu. Les aveugles voient. Ceux qui ne pouvaient pas marcher marchent. Les gens qui avaient une maladie de peau sont guéris et redeviennent purs. Les sourds entendent. Les morts reviennent à la vie. Et les pauvres entendent la bonne nouvelle.

decisions.choice: the list echoes Isaiah's promises of what God would do
decisions.reason: Isaiah promised that the blind would see, the deaf hear and the lame leap (Isaiah 35:5-6; 29:18), that the dead would live (Isaiah 26:19), and that good news would come to the poor (Isaiah 61:1, read by Jesus in 4:18). Jesus answers John's question with the deeds the prophets promised.

decisions.choice: lepers: people with a skin disease that made them unclean under the law
alternatives: people with the disease now called leprosy only
decisions.reason: As in 5:12, the word covered several skin diseases (Leviticus 13). Healing meant they could be declared clean and return to their community.

decisions.choice: the poor have good news proclaimed: the climax of the list
decisions.reason: The list ends with the poor, as in Jesus's reading of Isaiah (4:18). The verb is the one for telling good news (1:19; 3:18).

decisions.choice: people with skin diseases
decisions.reason: As in 5:12, Readable describes the disease instead of naming it.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:23
decisions.reason: Jesus's answer runs on into 7:23.

decisions.choice: la bonne nouvelle at every level
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the Gospels: where the English says "good news" French says "la bonne nouvelle" at every level. Here the Greek is a verb, "to have good news announced", and the climax of the list (m3) is that the poor hear it, not a name for the message.

decisions.choice: purifiés (L); rendus purs (B)
decisions.reason: As in Mark: the verb is the one for making clean under the law (m2), so French uses "pur, purifier" and not only "guérir"; Readable says both, as the English does.

source.text: καὶ μακάριός ἐστιν ὃς ἐὰν μὴ σκανδαλισθῇ ἐν ἐμοί.

records.literal_gloss: And blessed is whoever not is caused to stumble in me.

en.L: And blessed is whoever is not caused to stumble because of {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: And blessed is anyone who does not find in {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} a reason to fall away."
en.R: How blessed is anyone who does not stumble and turn away because of what I do!"

fr.L: Et heureux est celui qui ne trébuchera pas à cause de {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}}. »
fr.B: Heureux celui qui ne trouve pas en {{deity_pronoun:moi|Moi}} une raison de se détourner. »
fr.R: Heureux celui qui ne trébuche pas et ne se détourne pas à cause de ce que je fais ! »

decisions.choice: caused to stumble: tripped up, so as to turn away from Jesus
decisions.reason: The verb comes from the word for a trap or a stumbling block. It means to be led to fall away, not just to feel hurt. Jesus does not fit what some expect (7:34), and they turn from him.

decisions.choice: blessed: fortunate in God's eyes
decisions.reason: The word is the one of the blessings in 6:20-22.

decisions.choice: because of what I do
decisions.reason: Readable links the saying to the deeds of 7:22, which did not look like the judgment John announced.

decisions.choice: How blessed is anyone
decisions.reason: Readable makes the declaration an exclamation, as in 6:20.

decisions.choice: heureux at every level
decisions.reason: The word means fortunate in God's eyes (m2). French "béni" belongs to another Greek word, "blessed" by God or by people; "bienheureux" now sounds like church language. "Heureux celui qui …" is the French form of a declaration of happiness, as in the Beatitudes of 6:20-22.

source.text: Ἀπελθόντων δὲ τῶν ἀγγέλων Ἰωάννου ἤρξατο λέγειν πρὸς τοὺς ὄχλους περὶ Ἰωάννου· Τί ἐξήλθατε εἰς τὴν ἔρημον θεάσασθαι;

records.literal_gloss: Having departed then the messengers of John he began to speak to the crowds concerning John, What did you go out into the wilderness to look at?

en.L: When John's messengers had left, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} began to speak to the crowds about John: "What did you go out into the wilderness to look at?
en.B: After John's messengers had gone, Jesus began to talk to the crowds about John. "What did you go out into the wilderness to see?
en.R: When John's messengers had left, Jesus began to talk to the crowds about John. He said, "When you went out into the desert to see John, what did you expect to see?

fr.L: Les messagers de Jean étant partis, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} se mit à parler aux foules au sujet de Jean : « Qu’êtes-vous sortis regarder dans le désert ?
fr.B: Après le départ des messagers de Jean, Jésus se mit à parler de Jean aux foules : « Qu’êtes-vous allés voir au désert ?
fr.R: Quand les messagers de Jean sont partis, Jésus a commencé à parler de Jean aux foules. Il a dit : « Quand vous êtes allés dans le désert pour voir Jean, qu’est-ce que vous vous attendiez à voir ?

decisions.choice: messengers: people sent with a message
decisions.reason: The word can mean angel, but here it is John's two disciples. Jesus will use the same word of John himself in 7:27.

decisions.choice: the wilderness: the dry country near the Jordan where John preached
decisions.reason: Crowds went out to hear John and be baptized (3:2-7).

decisions.choice: to look at: to gaze at, as at a sight
decisions.reason: The verb means to look closely at something worth seeing.

decisions.choice: Jesus
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name Jesus at the start of a new section.

decisions.choice: the quotation opens here and closes at the end of 7:28
decisions.reason: Jesus's words about John run on through 7:28.

decisions.choice: desert
decisions.reason: Readable uses the everyday word for dry, empty country.

decisions.choice: le désert at every level
decisions.reason: As in Mark: French "désert" covers the empty, dry country by the Jordan (m2), not only sand, so one word serves every level where English needs "wilderness" and "desert".

source.text: κάλαμον ὑπὸ ἀνέμου σαλευόμενον;

records.literal_gloss: A reed by wind being shaken?

en.L: A reed being shaken by [the] wind?
en.B: A reed swaying in the wind?
en.R: A tall reed that the wind blows back and forth?

fr.L: Un roseau agité par le vent ?
fr.B: Un roseau qui plie au vent ?
fr.R: Un grand roseau que le vent fait pencher d’un côté et de l’autre ?

decisions.choice: a reed shaken by the wind: a weak, changeable person
alternatives: the actual reeds along the Jordan only
decisions.reason: Reeds grew thick along the Jordan, and people would have seen them. But a reed that bends with every wind is also a picture of weakness (1 Kings 14:15; 2 Kings 18:21). John was no such man; he spoke the same hard truth to everyone, even Herod (3:19).

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question is ironic: no one went out to the wilderness to stare at reeds.

source.text: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: But what did you go out to see?

en.L: But what did you go out to see?
en.B: If not, what did you go out to see?
en.R: What else did you expect to see?

fr.L: Mais qu’êtes-vous sortis voir ?
fr.B: Sinon, qu’êtes-vous allés voir ?
fr.R: Qu’est-ce que vous vous attendiez à voir d’autre ?

decisions.choice: but: if not that, then what?
decisions.reason: The word sets aside the answer just suggested and asks again.

source.text: ἄνθρωπον ἐν μαλακοῖς ἱματίοις ἠμφιεσμένον;

records.literal_gloss: A man in soft garments having been dressed?

en.L: A man dressed in soft clothing?
en.B: A man dressed in soft, fine clothes?
en.R: A man wearing soft, expensive clothes?

fr.L: Un homme vêtu de vêtements doux ?
fr.B: Un homme habillé de vêtements fins et luxueux ?
fr.R: Un homme qui porte des habits doux et très chers ?

decisions.choice: soft clothing: fine, costly clothing worn by the rich
decisions.reason: Soft cloth was a sign of wealth and an easy life. John wore clothing of camel's hair (Matthew 3:4).

source.text: ἰδοὺ οἱ ἐν ἱματισμῷ ἐνδόξῳ καὶ τρυφῇ ὑπάρχοντες ἐν τοῖς βασιλείοις εἰσίν.

records.literal_gloss: Look, those in clothing splendid and in luxury living in the palaces are.

en.L: Look, those who live in splendid clothing and luxury are in the royal palaces.
en.B: Those who wear splendid clothes and live in luxury are found in the palaces of kings.
en.R: People who wear fine clothes and live in luxury are in the palaces of kings.

fr.L: Voici, ceux qui vivent dans des vêtements somptueux et dans le luxe sont dans les palais royaux.
fr.B: Ceux qui portent des vêtements magnifiques et vivent dans le luxe, on les trouve dans les palais des rois.
fr.R: Les gens qui portent de beaux habits et qui vivent dans le luxe habitent dans les palais des rois.

decisions.choice: palaces: the courts of kings, such as Herod's
decisions.reason: Herod Antipas had John imprisoned (3:19-20). The men of the palace dressed in fine clothes; the prophet of the wilderness was locked up by them.

decisions.choice: look (L); not rendered as a separate word, or "now" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word to draw attention to what follows. "Behold" is old-fashioned; Literal says "look", and Balanced and Readable carry the force in the flow of the sentence, as in Matthew 1:20.

source.text: ἀλλὰ τί ἐξήλθατε ἰδεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: But what did you go out to see?

en.L: But what did you go out to see?
en.B: Then what did you go out to see?
en.R: So what did you go out to see?

fr.L: Mais qu’êtes-vous sortis voir ?
fr.B: Alors, qu’êtes-vous allés voir ?
fr.R: Alors, qu’est-ce que vous êtes allés voir ?

decisions.choice: the question asked a third time
decisions.reason: The repeated question builds to the real answer.

source.text: προφήτην;

records.literal_gloss: A prophet?

en.L: A prophet?
en.B: A prophet?
en.R: Did you go to see a prophet?

fr.L: Un prophète ?
fr.B: Un prophète ?
fr.R: Êtes-vous allés voir un prophète ?

decisions.choice: a prophet: one who speaks God's message
alternatives: one who only predicts the future
decisions.reason: The people took John for a prophet (20:6). No prophet had arisen in Israel for a long time.

decisions.choice: Did you go to see
decisions.reason: Readable makes the question a full sentence.

source.text: ναί, λέγω ὑμῖν, καὶ περισσότερον προφήτου.

records.literal_gloss: Yes, I say to you, and more than a prophet.

en.L: Yes, I tell you, and more than a prophet.
en.B: Yes, I tell you, and far more than a prophet.
en.R: Yes, he is a prophet. But I tell you, he is even more than a prophet.

fr.L: Oui, je vous le dis, et plus qu’un prophète.
fr.B: Oui, je vous le dis, et bien plus qu’un prophète.
fr.R: Oui, c’est un prophète. Mais je vous le dis, il est même plus qu’un prophète.

decisions.choice: more than a prophet: greater in his task than all the prophets before him
decisions.reason: John is himself the messenger the prophets foretold, as the next verse shows (1:76).

decisions.choice: he is a prophet. But
decisions.reason: Readable spells out what "yes" agrees with.

source.text: οὗτός ἐστιν περὶ οὗ γέγραπται· Ἰδοὺ ἀποστέλλω τὸν ἄγγελόν μου πρὸ προσώπου σου, ὃς κατασκευάσει τὴν ὁδόν σου ἔμπροσθέν σου.

records.literal_gloss: This is [he] concerning whom it has been written, Look, I send the messenger of me before face of you, who will prepare the way of you before you.

en.L: This is [the one] about whom it is written: 'Look, I send {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger before {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} face, who will prepare {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} way before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'
en.B: He is the one of whom Scripture says, 'I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger to go before {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; he will make {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} road ready ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'
en.R: John is the one the Scriptures speak about. There God says to the one who is to come, 'I am sending {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} messenger ahead of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. He will get the road ready for {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}.'

fr.L: Celui-ci est [celui] dont il est écrit : “Voici, j’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} face, qui préparera {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.”
fr.B: C’est de lui que l’Écriture dit : “J’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}} ; il préparera {{deity_pronoun:ton|Ton}} chemin devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.”
fr.R: Jean est celui dont parlent les Écritures. Là, Dieu dit à celui qui doit venir : “J’envoie {{deity_pronoun:mon|Mon}} messager devant {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}. Il préparera la route pour {{deity_pronoun:toi|Toi}}.”

decisions.choice: Malachi 3:1, with words from Exodus 23:20
decisions.reason: In Malachi 3:1 God says, "I send my messenger, and he will prepare the way before me." The words "before your face" come from Exodus 23:20, where God sends his angel before Israel. Mark 1:2 and Matthew 11:10 quote the same words.

decisions.choice: you and your: God speaks to the one who is to come, that is, to Jesus
decisions.reason: In Malachi the messenger prepares the way before the LORD himself. In Luke's quotation God speaks to another, and the messenger prepares that one's way. So the coming of Jesus is the coming of the LORD that Malachi promised (compare 1:76; 3:4). This answers John's question of 7:19.

decisions.choice: my messenger: God is the speaker
decisions.reason: In Malachi the speaker is the LORD of hosts. John is the messenger God sends.

decisions.choice: messenger: the same word as in 7:24
decisions.reason: John sent messengers to Jesus; John himself is God's messenger.

decisions.choice: my (God speaking) and you, your (spoken to Jesus), with the capital-pronoun setting
decisions.reason: God speaks of himself, and he speaks to Jesus, so both take the capital-pronoun setting. "He" is the messenger, John, and takes no setting.

decisions.choice: There God says to the one who is to come
decisions.reason: Readable names the speaker and the one spoken to, as the meaning decisions explain.

decisions.choice: to go before you (B); before your face (L)
decisions.reason: "Before your face" is a Hebrew way of saying "ahead of you". Literal keeps it.

decisions.choice: "j’envoie" without a span; "mon" (God), "ta", "ton", "toi" (Jesus) with the capital-pronoun setting
decisions.reason: As the English: God speaks of himself and to Jesus, so their pronouns take the setting; "il", the messenger, is John and takes none. French writes "je" for God without a span, as it does for Jesus.

source.text: λέγω ὑμῖν, μείζων ἐν γεννητοῖς γυναικῶν Ἰωάννου οὐδείς ἐστιν· ὁ δὲ μικρότερος ἐν τῇ βασιλείᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ μείζων αὐτοῦ ἐστιν.

records.literal_gloss: I say to you, greater among born of women than John no one is; the but least in the kingdom of the God greater than him is.

en.L: I tell you, among those born of women no one is greater than John; but the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he."
en.B: I tell you, of all who have been born of women, there is none greater than John. Yet the least in the kingdom of God is greater than he is."
en.R: I tell you, no one who has ever been born is greater than John. But even the least important person in the kingdom of God is greater than he is."

fr.L: Je vous le dis, parmi ceux qui sont nés de femmes, nul n’est plus grand que Jean ; mais le plus petit dans le royaume de Dieu est plus grand que lui. »
fr.B: Je vous le dis : de tous les êtres nés d’une femme, aucun n’est plus grand que Jean. Pourtant, le plus petit dans le royaume de Dieu est plus grand que lui. »
fr.R: Je vous le dis, aucun être humain n’a jamais été plus grand que Jean. Mais même celui qui est le moins important dans le royaume de Dieu est plus grand que lui. »

decisions.choice: among those born of women: among all human beings
alternatives: among the sons of mothers only
decisions.reason: The phrase is a Hebrew way of saying all people (Job 14:1).

decisions.choice: the least: the one of lowest rank
alternatives: the lesser one, meaning Jesus, who came after John
decisions.reason: The word is a comparative, "lesser", which here has the force of "least". Some readers in the early church took it to mean Jesus, younger than John and seen as lesser. But the contrast is between all who have lived and anyone in the kingdom of God.

decisions.choice: greater than John: not in character, but in what God has given
alternatives: John is shut out of the kingdom
decisions.reason: John stands at the turning point, the last and greatest of those who announced what was coming (16:16). To share in the kingdom that has now come with Jesus is a greater gift than even John's great task.

decisions.choice: no one who has ever been born
decisions.reason: Readable says what the idiom means.

decisions.choice: the quotation closes here and opens again in 7:31
decisions.reason: 7:29-30 are the narrator's words, as the decision on 7:29 explains.

decisions.choice: le royaume de Dieu at every level (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the New Testament. "Règne" would stress the reign over the realm; "royaume" is the familiar French term and covers both, as "kingdom" does.

source.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ λαὸς ἀκούσας καὶ οἱ τελῶναι ἐδικαίωσαν τὸν θεόν, βαπτισθέντες τὸ βάπτισμα Ἰωάννου·

records.literal_gloss: And all the people having heard and the tax collectors declared righteous the God, having been baptized [with] the baptism of John;

en.L: And all the people who heard, even the tax collectors, justified God, having been baptized with the baptism of John;
en.B: All the people who heard this, even the tax collectors, agreed that God was in the right, because they had been baptized with John's baptism.
en.R: All the people who heard Jesus say this agreed that God's way was right. Even the tax collectors agreed. They were the ones who had let John baptize them.

fr.L: Et tout le peuple qui entendit, et même les collecteurs d’impôts, justifièrent Dieu, ayant été baptisés du baptême de Jean ;
fr.B: Tout le peuple qui l’entendit, même les collecteurs d’impôts, reconnut que Dieu était dans son droit, car ils avaient été baptisés du baptême de Jean.
fr.R: Tous les gens qui ont entendu Jésus dire cela ont reconnu que le chemin de Dieu était le bon. Les collecteurs d’impôts aussi l’ont reconnu. C’étaient eux qui s’étaient fait baptiser par Jean.

decisions.choice: 7:29-30 are the narrator's comment, not part of Jesus's speech
decisions.reason: The SBLGNT does not use quotation marks, but it ends Jesus's words with a full stop at 7:28 and starts a new paragraph at 7:31, where Jesus asks another question. 7:29-30 tell, in the past tense, how two groups had responded to John, which is how Luke the narrator speaks (compare 3:10-14 and 20:4-7). Some read the verses as Jesus's own words; the meaning would not change.

decisions.choice: justified God: declared that God was right
decisions.reason: The verb means to declare someone in the right. The people acknowledged that God's way, shown in John's call to repent, was right. The same verb returns in 7:35.

decisions.choice: who heard: who heard Jesus's words about John
decisions.reason: The verb has no object. Jesus has just spoken about John to the crowds (7:24), and the people who had accepted John's baptism agreed.

decisions.choice: tax collectors: Jews who collected taxes for Rome or its rulers, and were despised
decisions.reason: As in 3:12 and 5:27-30, these were people others looked down on. They had come to John to be baptized (3:12).

decisions.choice: agreed that God was in the right (B); agreed that God's way was right (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what "justifying" God means, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: heard Jesus say this
decisions.reason: Readable says what they heard, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: justifièrent Dieu (L); reconnut que Dieu était dans son droit (B); ont reconnu que le chemin de Dieu était le bon (R)
alternatives: déclarèrent Dieu juste (B), as the style guide's term for justification
decisions.reason: Here it is God who is "justified": people declare that he is right (m2). The style guide's "déclarer juste" is for God declaring people righteous; used of God it would sound as if they judged him. Literal keeps the verb; Balanced and Readable say what it means, as the English does.

decisions.choice: les collecteurs d’impôts (for the whole chapter)
decisions.reason: As the style guide sets for the New Testament: "publicains" is a church word that most readers no longer understand.

source.text: οἱ δὲ Φαρισαῖοι καὶ οἱ νομικοὶ τὴν βουλὴν τοῦ θεοῦ ἠθέτησαν εἰς ἑαυτούς, μὴ βαπτισθέντες ὑπ’ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: The but Pharisees and the lawyers the purpose of the God rejected for themselves, not having been baptized by him.

en.L: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law set aside the purpose of God for themselves, not having been baptized by him.
en.B: But the Pharisees and the experts in the law refused what God intended for them, since they had not let John baptize them.
en.R: But the Pharisees and the experts in God's law turned away from what God wanted to do for them. They would not let John baptize them.

fr.L: Mais les Pharisiens et les experts de la Loi rejetèrent pour eux-mêmes le dessein de Dieu, n’ayant pas été baptisés par lui.
fr.B: Mais les Pharisiens et les experts de la Loi refusèrent ce que Dieu voulait pour eux, puisqu’ils ne s’étaient pas fait baptiser par Jean.
fr.R: Mais les Pharisiens et les spécialistes de la Loi de Dieu ont refusé ce que Dieu voulait faire pour eux. Ils n’ont pas voulu que Jean les baptise.

decisions.choice: experts in the law: men trained in the law of Moses, much like the scribes
decisions.reason: Luke uses this word for the experts who taught and applied God's law (10:25; 11:45-52). Many were Pharisees.

decisions.choice: the purpose of God: God's plan, here his call to repent through John
decisions.reason: The noun means a plan or decision. Luke uses it of God's saving plan (Acts 2:23; 20:27).

decisions.choice: for themselves: the plan was meant for them, and they rejected it
decisions.reason: The phrase can go with "rejected" (they rejected it, to their own loss) or with "purpose" (God's purpose for them). Either way they turned down what God offered them.

decisions.choice: Pharisees: a movement of Jews devoted to keeping God's law in every part of life
decisions.reason: As explained at 5:17 and 6:2.

decisions.choice: experts in God's law (R); experts in the law (L, B)
decisions.reason: Today "lawyer" suggests courts and contracts. The word means someone expert in the law of Moses.

decisions.choice: John
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name John, so the reader does not think of Jesus.

decisions.choice: les experts de la Loi (L, B); les spécialistes de la Loi de Dieu (R)
decisions.reason: The word means men trained in the law of Moses (m1). "Juristes" suggests courts and contracts, "légistes" is rare, and "docteurs" now suggests medicine. The capital on "Loi" marks the Law of Moses; Readable adds "de Dieu", as the English does, and its wording stays close to the Readable term for the scribes, "les spécialistes de la Loi".

decisions.choice: par Jean (B, R); par lui (L)
decisions.reason: As the English: French "lui" could be read as Jesus, so Balanced and Readable name John.

source.text: Τίνι οὖν ὁμοιώσω τοὺς ἀνθρώπους τῆς γενεᾶς ταύτης, καὶ τίνι εἰσὶν ὅμοιοι;

records.literal_gloss: To what then will I liken the people of the generation this, and to what are they like?

en.L: "To what then shall I compare the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation, and what are they like?
en.B: Jesus went on, "Then how shall I picture the {{gender:people|men}} of this generation? What are they like?
en.R: Jesus continued, "How can I describe the {{gender:people|men}} who live today? What are they like?

fr.L: « À quoi donc comparerai-je les {{gender:gens|hommes}} de cette génération, et à quoi ressemblent-ils ?
fr.B: Jésus poursuivit : « À quoi donc vais-je comparer les {{gender:gens|hommes}} de cette génération ? À quoi ressemblent-ils ?
fr.R: Jésus a continué : « À quoi est-ce que je peux comparer les {{gender:gens|hommes}} d’aujourd’hui ? À quoi ressemblent-ils ?

decisions.choice: this generation: the people of Jesus's time, as a whole
alternatives: a period of thirty or forty years
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the people of his day who refused both John and himself (11:29-32; 17:25).

decisions.choice: two questions with one meaning
decisions.reason: The second question repeats the first, a Hebrew way of giving a saying weight.

decisions.choice: people: human beings, men and women
decisions.reason: The word means people in general.

decisions.choice: Jesus went on (B); Jesus continued (R)
decisions.reason: After the narrator's comment in 7:29-30, Balanced and Readable say that Jesus is speaking again. Literal only opens the quotation again.

decisions.choice: who live today
decisions.reason: Readable says what "generation" means here.

decisions.choice: les {{gender:gens|hommes}}
decisions.reason: The word means human beings, men and women (m3). "Les humains de cette génération" would sound like a statement about the species; "les gens" is the ordinary inclusive word, with the traditional "les hommes" as the alternative. The article stays outside the span, since both read naturally.

source.text: ὅμοιοί εἰσιν παιδίοις τοῖς ἐν ἀγορᾷ καθημένοις καὶ προσφωνοῦσιν ἀλλήλοις, ἃ λέγει· Ηὐλήσαμεν ὑμῖν καὶ οὐκ ὠρχήσασθε· ἐθρηνήσαμεν καὶ οὐκ ἐκλαύσατε·

records.literal_gloss: Like they are to children who in marketplace are sitting and calling to one another, which says, We played the flute for you and not you danced; we sang a lament and not you wept.

en.L: They are like children sitting in [the] marketplace and calling to one another, who say, 'We played the flute for you, and you did not dance; we sang a lament, and you did not weep.'
en.B: They are like small children who sit in the town square and shout to each other, 'We played wedding music on the flute for you, and you would not dance. We sang a funeral song, and you would not cry.'
en.R: They are like children sitting in the town square. They call out to each other, 'We played happy music on the flute for you, but you would not dance! We sang sad songs, but you would not cry!'

fr.L: Ils ressemblent à des enfants assis sur la place du marché et qui s’interpellent les uns les autres, qui disent : “Nous avons joué de la flûte pour vous, et vous n’avez pas dansé ; nous avons chanté un chant de deuil, et vous n’avez pas pleuré.”
fr.B: Ils sont comme de petits enfants assis sur la place, qui se lancent des appels les uns aux autres : “Nous avons joué pour vous un air de noce à la flûte, et vous n’avez pas voulu danser. Nous avons chanté un chant funèbre, et vous n’avez pas voulu pleurer.”
fr.R: Ils sont comme des enfants assis sur la place de la ville. Ils crient les uns aux autres : “Nous avons joué de la flûte pour vous, un air joyeux, mais vous n’avez pas voulu danser ! Nous avons chanté des chants tristes, mais vous n’avez pas voulu pleurer !”

decisions.choice: the marketplace: the open square of a town, where people met and children played
decisions.reason: Every town had an open space for buying, selling and meeting.

decisions.choice: played the flute, sang a lament: children playing at weddings and at funerals
decisions.reason: Flute music went with weddings and feasts; wailing songs went with funerals. The children want the others to play their game, but the others will join in neither. So the people of this generation would accept neither John nor Jesus.

decisions.choice: which says: what the children call out
decisions.reason: The singular "says" goes with the neuter plural "children", as Greek allows.

decisions.choice: wedding music (B), happy music (R); a funeral song (B), sad songs (R)
alternatives: played the flute; sang a lament
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of game the children were playing, as the meaning decision explains.

source.text: ἐλήλυθεν γὰρ Ἰωάννης ὁ βαπτιστὴς μὴ ἐσθίων ἄρτον μήτε πίνων οἶνον, καὶ λέγετε· Δαιμόνιον ἔχει·

records.literal_gloss: Has come for John the Baptist not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, A demon he has;

en.L: For John the Baptist has come not eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, 'He has a demon.'
en.B: For John the Baptist has come eating no bread and drinking no wine, and you say, 'There is a demon in him.'
en.R: John the Baptist came, and he went without bread and did not drink wine. And you said, 'He has a demon in him!'
